questions.question_text: Empathy as a psychiatric term means:

options.text: To feel the pain of the patient
To be sympathetic to the patient's needs
To describe the patient's symptoms objectively
To understand the patient's subjective experience by 'putting oneself into the patient's shoes'
Discussing the patient's problems in detail

correct_answer.text: To understand the patient's subjective experience by 'putting oneself into the patient's shoes'

correct_answers.text: To understand the patient's subjective experience by 'putting oneself into the patient's shoes'

questions.explanation: Empathy involves proceeding through an organized series of questions, rephrasing and reiterating until one is sure of what the patient is describing.

questions.question_text: Psychomotor agitation is characterized by:
questions.explanation: When psychomotor agitation is severe, the patient cannot sit for long but paces up and down.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true about 'stupor'?

options.text: It is seen only in severe depression
It can be caused by both psychiatric and neurological disorders
It never presents with excitement and over-activity

correct_answer.text: It can be caused by both psychiatric and neurological disorders

correct_answers.text: It can be caused by both psychiatric and neurological disorders

questions.explanation: The key features of stupor include mutism, immobility and occasionally over-activity. Stupor can be caused by both psychiatric and neurological disorders.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements are true about REM sleep, except:

options.text: It is also known as paradoxical sleep
An electroencephalogram (EEG) is characterized by sleep-spindles and K-complexes
It is part of the normal sleep pattern
An EEG shows relatively low-voltage activity

correct_answer.text: An electroencephalogram (EEG) is characterized by sleep-spindles and K-complexes

correct_answers.text: An electroencephalogram (EEG) is characterized by sleep-spindles and K-complexes

questions.explanation: Sleep-spindles and K-complexes are normally seen in stage 2 of sleep. In REM sleep, a relatively low-voltage EEG is seen.

questions.question_text: All of the following are true about somnambulism, except:

options.text: It is more common in children
It is more common in females
It occurs in stages 3 and 4 of sleep
It is not part of dreams
It does not occur during REM

correct_answer.text: It is more common in females

correct_answers.text: It is more common in females

questions.explanation: Somnambulism is more common in males.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not true about narcolepsy?

options.text: It is often associated with cataplexy
It can be associated with hypnagogic hallucinations
It is usually not associated with organic brain pathology
It may be associated with sleep paralysis

questions.explanation: Narcolepsy does not start in childhood but usually starts in adolescence.

questions.question_text: De´ja´vu:

options.text: Is characterized by a feeling of familiarity in unfamiliar circumstances
Is classified as a memory disorder
Is the opposite of jamais vu
Can be a presenting symptom of temporal lobe epilepsy
May be caused by cerebrovascular disease

correct_answer.text: Can be a presenting symptom of temporal lobe epilepsy

correct_answers.text: Can be a presenting symptom of temporal lobe epilepsy

questions.explanation: De´ja´vu is not primarily a memory disorder.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements are true about confabulation, except:

options.text: It is a falsification of memory occurring in clear consciousness
It is usually associated with organic brain damage
It is seen only in Korsakoff's syndrome
It has been described in patients with schizophrenia
Suggestibility is a common feature associated with it

correct_answer.text: It is seen only in Korsakoff's syndrome

correct_answers.text: It is seen only in Korsakoff's syndrome

questions.explanation: Although it is commonly seen in Korsakoff's syndrome, that is not the only condition in which confabulation is seen.

questions.question_text: All of the following are common features of Ganser syndrome, except:
questions.explanation: Histrionic personality traits are more common in Ganser syndrome.

questions.question_text: All of the following are examples of sensory distortions, except:
questions.explanation: Somatization is a process where physical symptoms are experienced in the absence of an adequate organic cause.

questions.question_text: Pareidolia:

options.text: Is not uncommon in normal people
Can be provoked by psychoactive drugs

questions.explanation: Pareidolia involves illusions and not hallucinations.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is not true about hallucinations?
questions.explanation: Hallucinations by definition occur without external stimuli.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements are true about auditory hallucinations, except:

options.text: They can occur in organic brain disorders
They always occur in the first person
They can occur in chronic alcohol abuse

correct_answer.text: They always occur in the first person

correct_answers.text: They always occur in the first person

questions.explanation: Auditory hallucinations can occur in a number of forms such as a running commentary, or voices talking to the patient in the first and third person.

questions.question_text: Charles Bonnet syndrome is associated with all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: Delirium has to be excluded to diagnose Charles Bonnet syndrome.

questions.question_text: Delirium tremens is characterized by all of the following, except:

options.text: Auditory hallucinations giving a running commentary

correct_answer.text: Auditory hallucinations giving a running commentary

correct_answers.text: Auditory hallucinations giving a running commentary

questions.explanation: Auditory hallucinations giving a running commentary are not characteristic of delirium tremens but of schizophrenia.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true about pseudo-hallucinations?

options.text: They are experienced as true perceptions
They are always suggestive of a morbid mental state

questions.explanation: Pseudohallucinations require voluntary creation.

questions.question_text: All of the following are examples of true hallucinations, except:
questions.explanation: Pareidolia involves illusions and not true hallucinations.

questions.question_text: All of the following are examples of primary delusional phenomena, except:
questions.explanation: Primary/autochthonous delusion is ultimately not understandable. Secondary delusions are understandable in terms of the patient's mood state and/or life history.

questions.question_text: All of the following are true about delusions, except:

options.text: They are held with strong conviction
They are out of keeping with the cultural background
They feature a lack of insight

questions.explanation: Delusions are not diagnostic of schizophrenia and can be seen in other functional and organic disorders.

questions.question_text: All of the following syndromes are examples of delusional misidentification, except:
questions.explanation: De Clérambault's syndrome is also known as the delusion of love.

questions.question_text: Hypochondriac delusions:

options.text: Can present as delusions of body odour
Can present as delusions of infestation
Can present as delusions of ugliness

questions.explanation: Hypochondriacal delusions can occur in schizophrenia.

questions.question_text: All of the following disorders are usually associated with overvalued ideas, except:
questions.explanation: An overvalued idea is an acceptable, comprehensible idea pursued by the patient beyond the boundaries of reason.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not an example of passivity phenomena?
questions.explanation: Passivity experiences are those events in the realm of sensation, feeling, drive, and volition that are experienced as made or influenced by others. They have been well described as delusions of control.

questions.question_text: Which of the following disorders is unlikely to present as a stupor?
questions.explanation: Stupor is a condition in which the patient is immobile, mute and unresponsive but appears to be fully conscious in that the eyes are usually open and follow external objects.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not an example of compulsive rituals?
questions.explanation: Mannerisms are repeated involuntary movements that appear to be goal directed.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a compulsive ritual?
questions.explanation: Satyriasis is a compulsive need in the male to engage in sexual intercourse.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a feature of formal thought disorder as described by Schneider?
questions.explanation: Mutism is complete loss of speech.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a negative symptom in schizophrenia?
questions.explanation: Delusions are classified as positive symptoms that respond well to treatment with neuroleptics compared with negative symptoms.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a first-rank symptom of schizophrenia?

options.text: Hallucinatory voices giving a running commentary

questions.explanation: Schneider described first-rank symptoms.

questions.question_text: All of the following are examples of disorders of form of speech, except:
questions.explanation: Dysarthria is defined as a difficulty in the articulation of speech.

questions.question_text: Which of the following delusions is not common in depressive illness?
questions.explanation: Delusions in depression are usually mood-congruent.

questions.question_text: All of the following are true about obsessions, except:

options.text: They are recognized by the individual as absurd
They may be associated with compulsions

questions.explanation: Obsessions are not overvalued ideas because the person retains insight.

questions.question_text: Which of the following determine the form of a delusion?
questions.explanation: Unlike form, which is dictated by the type of illness, content is determined by the emotional, social and cultural background of the patient.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not characteristic of thought processes in schizophrenia?
questions.explanation: Characteristically, circumstantial thinking occurs in epileptic patients, and is seen in other organic states and in mental retardation.

questions.question_text: All of the following are language disorders caused by organic brain disease, except:
questions.explanation: Word salad occurs in schizophrenia.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements are true about flight of ideas, except:

options.text: It can be associated with pressure of speech
It is similar to retardation of thinking

correct_answer.text: It is similar to retardation of thinking

correct_answers.text: It is similar to retardation of thinking

questions.explanation: Retardation of thinking is the opposite of the flight of ideas and is commonly seen in depression.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not true about verbigeration?

options.text: It is similar to word salad
It is seen in expressive dysphasia

correct_answer.text: It is similar to word salad

correct_answers.text: It is similar to word salad

questions.explanation: Word salad is characteristic of schizophrenia and verbigeration is seen in patients with expressive dysphasia.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true about over-inclusive thinking?

options.text: It is not associated with schizophrenia
It is more common in patients with chronic schizophrenia
It is similar to formal thought disorder
There is a lack of connection between consecutive thoughts
It is not seen in the majority of schizophrenia patients

correct_answer.text: It is similar to formal thought disorder

correct_answers.text: It is similar to formal thought disorder

questions.explanation: Fewer than half of patients with schizophrenia show over-inclusive thinking.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is not true about receptive dysphasia?

options.text: It is an inability to understand spoken speech
It is a loss of meaning of words
It is impaired fluency of speech
It is impaired writing and reading

correct_answer.text: It is impaired fluency of speech

correct_answers.text: It is impaired fluency of speech

questions.explanation: Speech is fluent in receptive dysphasia.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not true about pure word dumbness?

options.text: It is impaired understanding of spoken speech
Ability to understand writing is preserved
Ability to respond to comments is preserved
It is not local disturbance of speech muscles

correct_answer.text: It is impaired understanding of spoken speech

correct_answers.text: It is impaired understanding of spoken speech

questions.explanation: The ability to understand spoken speech is preserved in pure word dumbness.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is not true about alexithymia?

options.text: The term was coined by Sifneos
It was originally introduced to describe psychosomatic disorders
It is characterized by verbal expression of emotions
It is associated with somatoform disorders
It is associated with substance abuse disorders

correct_answer.text: It is characterized by verbal expression of emotions

correct_answers.text: It is characterized by verbal expression of emotions

questions.explanation: Alexithymia is characterized by difficulties in expressing and verbalizing emotions.

questions.question_text: Dissociative fugue states are characterized by all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: Fugue states are characterized by amnesia.

questions.question_text: Clouding of consciousness is characterized by a disturbance in all of the following areas, except:
questions.explanation: Clouding may be seen in many organic brain syndromes, drug and alcohol intoxication, head injury, and meningeal irritation.

questions.question_text: Which of the following disorders is most likely to present with constructional apraxia?

options.text: Spinal cord lesion at cervical level

questions.explanation: Spinal cord lesions are caused by cortical lesions.

questions.question_text: Formal thought disorder in schizophrenia has been explained by all of the following terms, except:
questions.explanation: Logoclonia describes the spastic repetition of syllables that occurs in Parkinson's disease.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true about autoscopy?

options.text: It is also known as the double phenomena
It is commonly seen in multiple personalities
It means that the patient sees him /herself and knows that it is him /her
It is seen in Charles Bonnet syndrome

correct_answer.text: It means that the patient sees him /herself and knows that it is him /her

correct_answers.text: It means that the patient sees him /herself and knows that it is him /her

questions.explanation: Autoscopy is also known as phantom mirror image (seeing oneself and knowing that it is oneself).

questions.question_text: Which of the following symptoms in schizophrenia is not a disturbance of boundaries of self?

options.text: Hearing one's own thoughts out loud

questions.explanation: Delusion is a false unshakable belief.

questions.question_text: Which of the following does not describe depersonalization?
questions.explanation: Depersonalization is not associated with loss or attenuation of personal identity.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not seen in depersonalization?

options.text: Distortions in the experience of time
Changes in the subjective experience of memory

questions.explanation: Loss of ego boundaries is seen in schizophrenia but the abnormality is not confined to schizophrenia.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not true about dysmorphophobia?

options.text: It usually starts in middle age
It is more common in females
It is less common in married people or those living with partners
There is frequent comorbidity with mood disorders
There is a high rate of attempted suicide

correct_answer.text: It usually starts in middle age

correct_answers.text: It usually starts in middle age

questions.explanation: Dysmorphophobia usually starts in adolescence.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not true about hypochondriasis?

options.text: It is a well known disease
It can present with an undue concern about minor pain
It can present with unreasonable fears about the likelihood of developing a serious illness
Only a minority of patients are seen by psychiatrists

correct_answer.text: It is a well known disease

correct_answers.text: It is a well known disease

questions.explanation: Hypochondriasis is a symptom, not a disease.

questions.question_text: Which of the following does not characterize a dissociative disorder?

options.text: Causation of the symptoms is always conscious
Symptoms may carry some sort of advantage to the patient
An environmental stress factor might be present

correct_answer.text: Causation of the symptoms is always conscious

correct_answers.text: Causation of the symptoms is always conscious

questions.explanation: The causation of the symptoms is unconscious.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a feature of anorexia nervosa?
questions.explanation: The body weight is 15% lower than expected.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not true about phantom limb?

options.text: It is a distortion of body image
It is a rare occurrence in amputees
The amputee is aware of the phantom limb in space
The amputee can experience pain in the phantom limb
The phantom limb can change size with the passage of time

correct_answer.text: It is a rare occurrence in amputees

correct_answers.text: It is a rare occurrence in amputees

questions.explanation: Phantom limb phenomena occur in the majority of amputees.

questions.question_text: In transsexualism, the preoccupation with changing one's sex is:
questions.explanation: Transsexual people's belief that they are of the opposite sex is an overvalued idea taken to the extreme.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not true about phobias?

options.text: A phobia is a fear of a particular object or situation
The fear is out of proportion to the demands of the situation
The subject understands that the fear is irrational and senseless
The fear can be explained or reasoned away
The fear leads to avoidance of the situation

correct_answer.text: The fear can be explained or reasoned away

correct_answers.text: The fear can be explained or reasoned away

questions.explanation: In phobias the fear cannot be explained or reasoned away.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a symptom of agoraphobia?

options.text: Fear of eating in the presence of others

questions.explanation: A symptom of agoraphobia is a marked, consistent fear in or avoidance of at least two of the following situations: crowds, public places, travelling alone, travelling away from home.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a motor disorder seen in schizophrenia?
questions.explanation: Cataplexy is seen in sleep disorder; in narcolepsy, the subject falls down because of sudden loss of muscle tone provoked by strong emotion.

questions.question_text: The term 'schizophrenia' was coined by:
questions.explanation: Swiss psychiatrist Eugen Bleuler coined the term 'schizophrenia' in 1911.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a mood-congruent delusion in depression?
questions.explanation: Delusion of control is a passivity phenomenon seen in schizophrenia.

questions.question_text: A patient with schizophrenia saying 'Everybody knows what I am thinking' is having:
questions.explanation: Thought broadcast is also known as thought sharing or diffusion of thought.

questions.question_text: An elderly woman refusing to accept that her husband died of a heart attack 3 days ago is most likely to have:
questions.explanation: Morbid grief is associated with phobic avoidance, extreme guilt and anger, total lack of grieving, physical illness, and recurrent nightmares about the deceased.

questions.question_text: A patient with depression who says 'I feel as if I have no feelings' is having:
questions.explanation: All the others are seen mainly in schizophrenia.

questions.question_text: An elderly man suffering from depression who reports 'My heart has stopped and the blood is not flowing in my veins' is having which of the following phenomena?
questions.explanation: Bizarre nihilistic and hypochondriacal delusions in elderly people are associated with Cotard's syndrome.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not true about factitious disorder?

options.text: It features physical symptoms without an underlying cause
It features symptoms not under the voluntary control of the individual
It is a need to assume the sick role
It has no obvious economic gain

correct_answer.text: It features symptoms not under the voluntary control of the individual

correct_answers.text: It features symptoms not under the voluntary control of the individual

questions.explanation: Factitious disorder refers to self-inflicted signs and symptoms. It differs from malingering in that it does not bring any external reward such as financial compensation.

questions.question_text: A teenage girl seeking plastic surgery because of the small size of her breasts is likely to have which of the following?
questions.explanation: Dysmorphophobia is sometimes described by schizophrenia patients.

questions.question_text: Delusions of infestation are also known as:
questions.explanation: In Munchausen syndrome, the person intentionally fakes an illness. All the others are delusional disorders.

questions.question_text: A patient who believes that strangers are actually close relatives in disguise is having which of the following?
questions.explanation: False identification of strangers as familiar people occurs in Fregoli syndrome.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not associated with pseudologia fantastica?
questions.explanation: Pseudologia fantastica is pathological lying.

questions.question_text: Doctor to a patient with Alzheimer's disease: 'How old are you?' Patient: '67 years.' Doctor: 'Where do you come from?' Patient: '67 years.' Which phenomenon is the patient exhibiting?
questions.explanation: Perseveration is a sign of organic brain disease, perhaps the only pathognomonic sign in psychiatry.

questions.question_text: A patient with schizophrenia reports that each time a fellow patient sneezes he feels severe pain in his tummy. Which type of hallucinatory phenomena is he exhibiting?
questions.explanation: A hallucinatory form of synaesthesia, reflex hallucination is described as a stimulus in one sensory modality producing a hallucination in another.

questions.question_text: Which of the following does not fit into the description of Cotard's syndrome?
questions.explanation: Cotard's syndrome is associated with agitated depression.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements best describes the meaning of anhedonia?
questions.explanation: Anhedonia is a core symptom of depression.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not true about autochthonous delusions?

options.text: They can be preceded by delusional mood
They can be a source of secondary delusions
They are also known as 'brain waves'

questions.explanation: Autochthonous delusions, although common in schizophrenia, are not pathognomonic of schizophrenia.

questions.question_text: All of the following are recognized characteristics of schizoid personality disorder, except:

options.text: A greater likelihood of developing schizophrenia
Poor capacity to form social relationships
A tendency to break the law
Indifference to the feelings of other people

correct_answer.text: A tendency to break the law

correct_answers.text: A tendency to break the law

questions.explanation: Schizoid personalities do not have a tendency to break the law, which is a more common feature of antisocial personalities.

questions.question_text: Unstable interpersonal relationships, impulsivity and recurrent suicidal behaviour are part of which of the following personality disorders?
questions.explanation: Individuals with unstable personality disorder use less mature defence mechanisms, such as projection and denial.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true about pseudohallucinations?

options.text: They cannot occur in normal people
They are subject to conscious manipulation
They cannot have a definite outline and vivid detail

questions.explanation: Pseudohallucinations arise in inner space as opposed to true hallucinations, which occur in objective space.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a feature of catatonic schizophrenia?
questions.explanation: Coprolalia is the obscene utterances commonly seen in Tourette's syndrome.

questions.question_text: Which of the following symptoms is unlikely to be seen in stupor?
questions.explanation: The characteristic presentation of stupor is a lack of reaction to, and unawareness of surroundings. Unconsciousness is not a feature.

questions.question_text: Ganser syndrome is commonly seen in:
questions.explanation: In Ganser syndrome approximate answers, clouding of consciousness with disorientation, hysterical stigmata, recent history of head injury/typhus/severe emotional stress, pseudohallucinations and amnesia are present.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a feature of Tourette's syndrome?
questions.explanation: Choreiform movements are not a feature of Tourette's syndrome but are commonly seen in Huntington's chorea and other neurological disorders.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not an illusion?
questions.explanation: Misinterpretation means simply making a mistake.
